title: Outcome/adoption dashboard (reads the ledger)
context: The outcome ledger (task-019) records adoption events, teacher feedback, and reuse data per plan. Reading the ledger manually is feasible at small scale, but as the plan library grows, a summary dashboard becomes valuable: showing which plans are adopted, adoption rates, usefulness ratings, reuse events, and cycle-time trends. The dashboard supports success-metric reporting to stakeholders and the public. It must read from the outcome ledger without collecting new data, emit no student or teacher PII, and be a static or server-free view (no student-facing platform).
objective: Build a read-only outcome and adoption dashboard that reads the committed outcome ledger and displays key success metrics (plans authored, adopted, usefulness ratings, reuse events) without collecting or exposing PII.
acceptanceCriteria: Dashboard reads from the committed outcome ledger (teacher-lesson-plans-feedback-019) and displays at minimum: total plans published, total plans adopted (taught or repository-accepted), adoption rate, average usefulness rating, and number of verified reuse events.
Dashboard emits no PII: teacher/partner names are shown only at the level the outcome ledger records (name/org if consented, otherwise aggregated/anonymous).
Dashboard is static or server-free: it generates a static HTML/JSON report from the ledger file (no backend, no database, no runtime server that collects data).
Dashboard is committed to the repo and runs as a CI step (regenerated on ledger changes); the output static report is committed or published to GitHub Pages.
Code is MIT-licensed; pnpm build && pnpm test && pnpm lint pass; no credentials embedded.
resources: teacher-lesson-plans-scale-018 — scale library (plans to report on)
PLAN.md — §Success metrics (the metrics the dashboard must display)
PLAN.md — §Data, licensing & compliance (Privacy / PII — no PII in outputs)
output: A merged PR adding a static outcome/adoption dashboard that reads the outcome ledger and displays key success metrics, with CI integration and no PII exposure.
